TOPSIS Centrality

Source: R/centrality-batch65.R
centrality_topsis.Rd

TOPSIS centrality (Du et al. 2014) ranks nodes by their closeness to an ideal node on three centrality measures at once. Each measure is divided by its Euclidean norm over the nodes and multiplied by its weight; the ideal node has the largest value on every measure and the anti-ideal node the smallest. With \(S^+_i\) and \(S^-_i\) the Euclidean distances of node \(i\) to the two, $$C_i = \frac{S^-_i}{S^-_i + S^+_i}.$$ The measures are degree, closeness and either betweenness or eigenvector centrality.

Usage

centrality_topsis(x, ...)

Arguments

x

Network input accepted by centrality.

...

Further arguments to centrality. The measure uses topsis_attribute (\"betweenness\" or \"eigenvector\") and topsis_weights (three weights, default one third each).

Value

A named numeric vector with one score per node, in input node order.

Details

The measure is computed on the simple undirected skeleton of the network, so direction, weights, loops and parallel edges are ignored. topsis_attribute names the third measure: "betweenness" (the default), which the source uses where traffic follows shortest paths, or "eigenvector", which it uses where traffic spreads along walks. topsis_weights holds the weights of degree, closeness and the third measure. The default is one third each: the source states no weights for networks, and uses equal weights in its only numerical illustration. Only the proportions of the weights matter. The score lies in \([0, 1]\). It has no value on a disconnected network, where closeness is undefined, on a one-node network, and on a network whose nodes are all equal on the three measures (a measure whose range is within 1e-12 of its largest value counts as equal); there the measure warns (class cograph_undefined_measure) and returns NA. The source prints no score of a network node; the implementation reproduces the distances and the ranking of its numerical illustration. centrality_topsis_re is a later variant with four measures, fixed weights and a relative-entropy distance. The weighted TOPSIS of Hu et al. (2016) is this measure with the betweenness and weights taken from a simulated spreading process; given those weights through topsis_weights, it gives the same scores. Its weight rule is not built in: the spreading values it prints do not follow from the model it states, and the weights it gives change strongly from one simulation to the next. With the weights its worked example multiplies into the attributes, topsis_weights = c(0.5824, 0.0705, 0.3471), the implementation reproduces the six scores and the ranking of its Table 2; the example prints these weights in the order degree, betweenness, closeness but applies them in the order degree, closeness, betweenness. An unknown topsis_attribute, or a topsis_weights that is not three finite nonnegative numbers, not all zero, raises a cograph_bad_parameter error. normalized = TRUE divides the scores by their maximum.

References

Du, Y., Gao, C., Hu, Y., Mahadevan, S. and Deng, Y. (2014). A new method of identifying influential nodes in complex networks based on TOPSIS. Physica A: Statistical Mechanics and its Applications, 399, 57-69. doi:10.1016/j.physa.2013.12.031 .

Hu, J., Du, Y., Mo, H., Wei, D. and Deng, Y. (2016). A modified weighted TOPSIS to identify influential nodes in complex networks. Physica A: Statistical Mechanics and its Applications, 444, 73-85. doi:10.1016/j.physa.2015.09.028 .

See also

centrality_topsis_re, centrality_betweenness, centrality_closeness, centrality.

Examples

centrality_topsis(regulation_net)
#>    Explore       Plan    Monitor      Adapt    Reflect    Discuss Synthesize 
#>  0.3203679  0.7310498  0.9747116  0.8595407  0.5758228  0.3317009  0.0000000 
#>   Evaluate     Create      Share 
#>  0.2230220  0.5622354  0.1898842 
centrality_topsis(regulation_net, topsis_attribute = "eigenvector")
#>    Explore       Plan    Monitor      Adapt    Reflect    Discuss Synthesize 
#>  0.3000748  0.6619468  1.0000000  0.6300121  0.2845016  0.3129138  0.0000000 
#>   Evaluate     Create      Share 
#>  0.3655761  0.6764735  0.3690224
